relation: the undirected Cayley graph of a supplied finite group and an arbitrary connection set: Extremal D2ram cayley_adj/cayley_graph and Hamilton U2 cayley_rel/cayley_graph (Sections over gT : finGroupType and S : {set gT}) are GTBase.cayley_graphs.undirected_cayley_rel/undirected_cayley_graph: the carrier gT and the loopless symmetrised relation (x != y) && ((x^-1 * y \in S) || (y^-1 * x \in S)) by conversion (U2's group_scope and D2ram's explicit %g elaborate to the same term); each graph agrees pointwise with undirected_cayley_graph and by the identity isomorphism. The four constructor proofs are related through the graphs they build (eq_diso), never by proof-field equality. No inverse closure, generation, abelianity or order condition is imposed on the primitive; the row guards stay in the rows.
summary: Batch A, family A26 (undirected Cayley graphs), on Arthur's A25 pin 5832ba9. New GTBase.cayley_graphs gives undirected_cayley_graph S : sgraph for any finite group gT and any S : {set gT}, with the loopless symmetrised relation (x != y) && ((x^-1 * y \in S) || (y^-1 * x \in S)): its adjacency view and #|gT| vertices, edges along right multiplication by S and by its inverses, the inverse-closed specialisation, and the empty, identity and full connection sets (edgeless, edgeless, complete). D2ram's cayley_adj/cayley_graph and U2's cayley_rel/cayley_graph are now aliases; their four constructor proofs are one-line uses of the public ones. The public client covers carrier and adjacency, the three connection sets, a group of order one, an arbitrary and an inverse-closed S, and a nonsymmetric example in the nonabelian group 'S_3.

Frozen verbatim at 5832ba9: the four sources and the four constructor proofs with their scripts, in dependency-ordered modules with each Section's scaffolding (U2's Local Open Scope group_scope included), U2's hamiltonian_cycle (with its Arguments), is_hamiltonian and symmetric_set, and the two complete rows: D2ram's Ramsey row (one positive c before every finite abelian group of order > 1, one inverse-closed S, both 2^omega and 2^alpha bounds for that graph) and U2's Hamiltonicity row (order > 2, S inverse-closed and generating, a Hamiltonian cycle). Thirteen mappings, two whole iffs; no Original was found on this parent.

Proof consumers: grounding_D2ram's cayley_adj_set0/cayley_adj_setT and grounding_U2's cayley_full add one unfold of the public relation with unchanged headers; implications_D2ram.D2ram_nodes_in_scope and the rest of the closure recompile unchanged. The directed Digraph.constructions.cayley.cayley stays distinct.
